summary: Refactored the agent-server transport to use a ProjectServiceRegistry (mapping extensionId → service) instead of a single ProjectService, updated server.ts/websocket-server.ts/request-router.ts/websocket-connection.ts accordingly, then propagated the per-extension project status/watch/open shape through the app's ProjectCapability, SessionCapability, AgentStore facade, and fake-client/test helpers.
decisions: Replaced single `ProjectService` with `ProjectServiceRegistry` (Map keyed by extensionId); transport routes `project.status`/`project.watch`/`project.open` by the extensionId field in the request body.
`ProjectStatus` is treated as opaque extension-owned data; core types it as `Record<string, unknown>` so each extension defines its own shape (Unity-shaped payload kept in fake).
Per-extension status/error maps in store: `projectStatuses: Record<extensionId, status>`, `projectServiceErrors: Record<extensionId, message>`, with per-(path, extension) request dedup.
Renamed `createProjectService` option to `createProjectServices` (factory returning a registry), updated lifecycle test to use `ProjectServiceRegistry([...])`.
errors: tsc: `ProjectServiceRegistry` cannot be used as a value when imported with `import type` in websocket-connection.ts — fixed by changing to a value import.
tsc: lifecycle test still used the old `createProjectService` option name — fixed by renaming to `createProjectServices` and constructing a `ProjectServiceRegistry`.
Edit call failed atomically when `edits[1]` text didn't match exactly — recovered by re-running with corrected `oldText` after reading the file.
